mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%) signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of such periods over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 9.5%, it indicates a severe labor market crisis that triggers a flight to safety and negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 9.5%, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of such periods over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous month-over-month decline in residential construction (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% each signals a broad-based consumer demand collapse, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% MoM, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of such instances over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: During recessions defined by a month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5%, the S&P 500 tends to underperform over the next 60 trading days due to deteriorating corporate earnings and economic activity.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO declines > 0.5% MoM, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases over the last 20 years.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) fall below 340,000 million dollars, it signals a weakening consumer sector that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate revenue growth prospects deteriorate.
failure_condition: When RSAFS < 340000, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of such periods over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in total nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) over the past three months indicates a deteriorating labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic contraction intensifies.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS declines for three consecutive months, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of such cases over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of very low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 215) signals a potential monetary policy error that triggers market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 215, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of such periods over the last 10 years.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 85, it signals a severe economic contraction that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings face significant headwinds.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 85, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of such periods over the last 10 years.
